evidence: Baseline eShopLegacyNTier WCF service lifecycle, EF model/database allocation, static state and project Compile lists reviewed. No custom lock acquisition or deployed singleton was found. UWP Singleton helper is excluded from compilation; ConcurrentDictionary presence alone is not a deployed singleton vulnerability. Shared resource is the database across WCF instances; no unsafe shared DbContext assertion made. No concurrency/load test or database access performed.

values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

values.name: Improper Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem reads the shared database maximum Id at line 67, increments it at line 68 and inserts at lines 69-70 without a transaction covering both read and insert or cross-instance synchronization. CatalogItem disables database-generated IDs at lines 13-15. Concurrent SOAP calls handled by separate WCF service instances can read the same maximum and attempt the same primary key; one insert can fail with a duplicate-key exception. WCF default per-instance single concurrency does not serialize access across all instances. A service-reachable actor issuing concurrent creations can induce intermittent legitimate write failures. Database primary-key constraints prevent duplicate committed identifiers; no data overwrite or lasting global outage established. Requires overlapping requests against the same database, not runtime reproduced. CWE-662 and CWE-820 are overlapping classifications of this missing atomicity, not two independent defects.

values.name: Improper Locking
values.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

values.name: Missing Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
